questions.questionText: An operation is defined by a # b = a + 2b. Find 7 # 5.
questions.explanationText: Substitute a=7 and b=5: 7 + 2×5 = 17.

questions.questionText: An operation is defined by a ★ b = 3a − b. Find 8 ★ 6.
questions.explanationText: Substitute a=8 and b=6: 3×8 − 6 = 18.

questions.questionText: An operation is defined by a ⊙ b = ab + a − b. Find 6 ⊙ 4.
questions.explanationText: Substitute a=6 and b=4: 6×4 + 6 − 4 = 26.

questions.questionText: An operation is defined by a △ b = a² + b. Find 5 △ 7.
questions.explanationText: Substitute a=5 and b=7: 5² + 7 = 32.

questions.questionText: An operation is defined by a ◇ b = b² − a. Find 9 ◇ 5.
questions.explanationText: Substitute a=9 and b=5: 5² − 9 = 16.

questions.questionText: An operation is defined by a @ b = (a + b) / 2. Find 11 @ 5.
questions.explanationText: Substitute a=11 and b=5: (11 + 5) / 2 = 8.

questions.questionText: An operation is defined by a ⊕ b = |a − b| + 3. Find -4 ⊕ 7.
questions.explanationText: Substitute a=-4 and b=7: |−4 − 7| + 3 = 14.

questions.questionText: An operation is defined by a % b = 2a + 3b. Find 4 % 9.
questions.explanationText: Substitute a=4 and b=9: 2×4 + 3×9 = 35.

questions.questionText: An operation is defined by a □ b = a² − 2b. Find 7 □ 8.
questions.explanationText: Substitute a=7 and b=8: 7² − 2×8 = 33.

questions.questionText: An operation is defined by a ♢ b = (a − b)². Find 3 ♢ 9.
questions.explanationText: Substitute a=3 and b=9: (3 − 9)² = 36.

questions.questionText: Find x if x # 4 = 23, where a # b = 3a + 2b.
Find x if 7 ★ x = 31, where a ★ b = 5a − b.
Find x if x ⊙ 3 = 28, where a ⊙ b = ab + a.
questions.explanationText: 3x + x = 28, so 4x = 28 and x = 7.

questions.questionText: Find x if 6 △ x = 20, where a △ b = a + 2b.
Find x if x ◇ 5 = 9, where a ◇ b = |a − b|, and x > 5.
questions.explanationText: |x−5|=9 gives x=14 or x=−4; the condition x>5 selects x=14.

If a ★ b = 2a − b, which expression has the value 14?
If a @ b = ab − a, which expression has the value 12?
If a △ b = a² + b², which expression has the value 29?
If a ◇ b = (a+b)/(a−b), which expression has the value 2?
Define a # b = a + 2b and a $ b = ab − 1. Evaluate (2 # 5) $ 3.
Define a * b = a + b + ab and a @ b = a² − b. Evaluate (2 * 3) @ 4.
Define a △ b = 2a − b and a ◇ b = a + b². Evaluate (9 △ 4) ◇ 2.
Define a ⊕ b = |a−b| and a ⊗ b = 3a+b. Evaluate (5 ⊕ 12) ⊗ 4.
Define a # b = a²+b and a % b = a−2b. Evaluate (4 # 3) % 5.
Define a @ b = (a+b)/2 and a $ b = 2a+b. Evaluate (8 @ 4) $ 7.
Define a □ b = ab+a and a ○ b = b−a. Evaluate (3 □ 4) ○ 20.
Define a ★ b = a+3b and a ♢ b = a²−b². Evaluate (1 ★ 4) ♢ 5.

Given a # b = a + 2b and a $ b = ab − 1, compare 2 # (5 $ 3) with (2 # 5) $ 3.
questions.explanationText: The first expression is 30 and the second is 35; therefore the exact relation is <.

questions.questionText: Given a * b = a + b + ab and a @ b = a² − b, compare 2 * (3 @ 4) with (2 * 3) @ 4.
questions.explanationText: The first expression is 17 and the second is 117; therefore the exact relation is <.

questions.questionText: Given a △ b = 2a − b and a ◇ b = a + b², compare 9 △ (4 ◇ 2) with (9 △ 4) ◇ 2.
questions.explanationText: The first expression is 10 and the second is 18; therefore the exact relation is <.

questions.questionText: Given a ⊕ b = |a−b| and a ⊗ b = 3a+b, compare 5 ⊕ (12 ⊗ 4) with (5 ⊕ 12) ⊗ 4.
questions.explanationText: The first expression is 35 and the second is 25; therefore the exact relation is >.

questions.questionText: Given a # b = a²+b and a % b = a−2b, compare 4 # (3 % 5) with (4 # 3) % 5.
questions.explanationText: The first expression is 9 and the second is 9; therefore the exact relation is =.

questions.questionText: Given a @ b = (a+b)/2 and a $ b = 2a+b, compare 8 @ (4 $ 7) with (8 @ 4) $ 7.
questions.explanationText: The first expression is 23/2 and the second is 19; therefore the exact relation is <.

questions.questionText: Given a □ b = ab+a and a ○ b = b−a, compare 3 □ (4 ○ 20) with (3 □ 4) ○ 20.
questions.explanationText: The first expression is 51 and the second is 5; therefore the exact relation is >.

questions.questionText: Given a ★ b = a+3b and a ♢ b = a²−b², compare 1 ★ (4 ♢ 5) with (1 ★ 4) ♢ 5.
questions.explanationText: The first expression is -26 and the second is 144; therefore the exact relation is <.

questions.questionText: Given a ▽ b = a−b/2 and a ▲ b = ab+2, compare 10 ▽ (6 ▲ 4) with (10 ▽ 6) ▲ 4.
questions.explanationText: The first expression is -3 and the second is 30; therefore the exact relation is <.

questions.questionText: Given a ⊙ b = a+b−1 and a ⊖ b = 2a−3b, compare 7 ⊙ (5 ⊖ 3) with (7 ⊙ 5) ⊖ 3.
questions.explanationText: The first expression is 7 and the second is 13; therefore the exact relation is <.

questions.questionText: # means the operation defined by a+b, and $ means ab. If $ before #, evaluate 8 # 3 $ 4.
@ means the operation defined by a−b, and ★ means a+2b. If ★ before @, evaluate 15 @ 4 ★ 3.
△ means the operation defined by a+3b, and ○ means a/b. If △ before ○, evaluate 6 △ 2 ○ 4.
□ means the operation defined by 2a+b, and ◇ means a−b. If □ before ◇, evaluate 5 □ 7 ◇ 3.
⊕ means the operation defined by a+b, and ⊗ means a²+b. If ⊗ before ⊕, evaluate 2 ⊕ 3 ⊗ 4.
# is defined by a+2b, and $ by a−b. Evaluate 7 # 3 $ 4 strictly from left to right.
questions.explanationText: Left to right: 7 # 3 = 13; then 13 $ 4 = 9.

questions.questionText: * is defined by ab+1, and @ by a+b. Evaluate 2 * 5 @ 3 strictly from left to right.

questions.questionText: △ is defined by a²−b, and ○ by 2a+b. Evaluate 5 △ 6 ○ 4 strictly from left to right.
questions.explanationText: Left to right: 5 △ 6 = 19; then 19 ○ 4 = 42.

questions.questionText: ⊕ is defined by |a−b|, and ◇ by a+3b. Evaluate 4 ⊕ 11 ◇ 2 strictly from left to right.
questions.explanationText: Left to right: 4 ⊕ 11 = 7; then 7 ◇ 2 = 13.

questions.questionText: □ is defined by a+b/2, and ★ by ab. Evaluate 9 □ 6 ★ 2 strictly from left to right.
questions.explanationText: Left to right: 9 □ 6 = 12; then 12 ★ 2 = 24.

questions.questionText: An operator ★ follows one rule in all cases: 2 ★ 3 = 13, 4 ★ 1 = 11, 1 ★ 2 = 8. Which value is consistent for 5 ★ 6?
questions.explanationText: The examples fit a ★ b = 2a + 3b. Hence 5 ★ 6 = 28.

questions.questionText: An operator ★ follows one rule in all cases: 3 ★ 2 = 11, 5 ★ 4 = 29, 1 ★ 2 = 3. Which value is consistent for 6 ★ 7?
questions.explanationText: The examples fit a ★ b = a² + b. Hence 6 ★ 7 = 43.

questions.questionText: An operator ★ follows one rule in all cases: 2 ★ 4 = 14, 3 ★ 5 = 23, 1 ★ 2 = 5. Which value is consistent for 6 ★ 2?
questions.explanationText: The examples fit a ★ b = ab + a + b. Hence 6 ★ 2 = 20.

questions.questionText: An operator ★ follows one rule in all cases: 5 ★ 3 = 16, 7 ★ 2 = 45, 1 ★ 2 = -3. Which value is consistent for 9 ★ 4?
questions.explanationText: The examples fit a ★ b = a² − b². Hence 9 ★ 4 = 65.

questions.questionText: An operator ★ follows one rule in all cases: 2 ★ 5 = 13, 6 ★ 3 = 21, 1 ★ 2 = 3. Which value is consistent for 4 ★ 9?
questions.explanationText: The examples fit a ★ b = |a−b| + ab. Hence 4 ★ 9 = 41.

questions.questionText: An operator ★ follows one rule in all cases: 4 ★ 1 = 10, 6 ★ 5 = 8, 1 ★ 2 = -1. Which value is consistent for 8 ★ 3?
questions.explanationText: The examples fit a ★ b = 3a − 2b. Hence 8 ★ 3 = 18.

questions.questionText: An operator ★ follows one rule in all cases: 3 ★ 7 = 5, 8 ★ 4 = 6, 1 ★ 2 = 3/2. Which value is consistent for 11 ★ 5?
questions.explanationText: The examples fit a ★ b = (a+b)/2. Hence 11 ★ 5 = 8.

questions.questionText: An operator ★ follows one rule in all cases: 3 ★ 2 = 9, 5 ★ 4 = 25, 1 ★ 2 = 3. Which value is consistent for 7 ★ 3?
questions.explanationText: The examples fit a ★ b = a(b+1). Hence 7 ★ 3 = 28.

questions.questionText: An operator ★ follows one rule in all cases: 2 ★ 5 = 14, 4 ★ 3 = 22, 1 ★ 2 = 5. Which value is consistent for 6 ★ 1?
questions.explanationText: The examples fit a ★ b = a² + 2b. Hence 6 ★ 1 = 38.

questions.questionText: An operator ★ follows one rule in all cases: 3 ★ 2 = 10, 4 ★ 5 = 35, 1 ★ 2 = 2. Which value is consistent for 6 ★ 3?
questions.explanationText: The examples fit a ★ b = 2ab − b. Hence 6 ★ 3 = 33.

questions.questionText: For a ★ b = a+b+ab, which description is correct?
questions.explanationText: Interchanging a and b leaves a+b+ab unchanged.

questions.questionText: For a ★ b = a−2b, which description is correct?

options.text: equal to b ★ a for all values

questions.explanationText: For example, 3★1=1 but 1★3=−5, so order matters.

questions.questionText: For a ★ b = |a−b|, which description is correct?
questions.explanationText: |a−b|=|b−a| for all real a and b.

questions.questionText: For a ★ b = a/b, b≠0, which description is correct?
questions.explanationText: Usually a/b differs from b/a; for instance 2/4≠4/2.

questions.questionText: For a ★ b = a²+b², which description is correct?
questions.explanationText: a²+b² is unchanged when the inputs are swapped.

questions.questionText: Given A > B, B ≥ C, C > D, which conclusion is strongest?
questions.explanationText: A>B≥C>D, so transitivity gives A>D.

questions.questionText: Given P ≤ Q, Q < R, R ≤ S, which conclusion is strongest?
questions.explanationText: P≤Q<R≤S, and the strict middle relation ensures P<S.

questions.questionText: Given K = L, L > M, M ≥ N, which conclusion is strongest?
questions.explanationText: K=L>M≥N, so K>N.

questions.questionText: Given X < Y, Y = Z, Z ≤ W, which conclusion is strongest?
questions.explanationText: X<Y=Z≤W, hence X<W.

questions.questionText: Given H ≥ J, J > K, K = T, which conclusion is strongest?
questions.explanationText: H≥J>K=T, so H>T.

questions.questionText: Given U < V, V ≤ W, W < Z, which conclusion is strongest?
questions.explanationText: Following the chain gives U<V≤W<Z, hence U<Z.

questions.questionText: Given R = S, S ≥ T, T > M, which conclusion is strongest?
questions.explanationText: R=S≥T>M, so R>M.

questions.questionText: Given C > D, D = E, E > F, which conclusion is strongest?
questions.explanationText: C>D=E>F, hence C>F.

questions.questionText: Given G ≤ H, H ≤ J, J < K, which conclusion is strongest?
questions.explanationText: G≤H≤J<K ensures G<K.

questions.questionText: Given B < C, C ≥ D, which conclusion is strongest?

options.text: relation between B and D cannot be determined

questions.explanationText: C exceeds B and is at least D, but B and D may be in either order or equal.

questions.questionText: Given a > b > 0, which statement is correct?
questions.explanationText: Since both are positive, squaring preserves their strict order.

questions.questionText: Given x < y < 0, which statement is correct?
questions.explanationText: The more negative x has larger absolute value, so x²>y².

questions.questionText: Given m > n with no sign information, which statement is correct?

options.text: m² and n² cannot be ordered with certainty

questions.explanationText: For example 2>1 gives m²>n², while −1>−2 gives m²<n².

questions.questionText: Given p ≥ q and q ≥ p, which statement is correct?
questions.explanationText: Both weak inequalities can hold together only when p=q.

questions.questionText: Given r > s and st > rt, which statement is correct?
questions.explanationText: st−rt=t(s−r)>0. Since s−r<0, t must be negative.

questions.questionText: Given u < v and uw > vw, which statement is correct?
questions.explanationText: Multiplication reversed the order, which occurs only for negative w.

questions.questionText: Given c > d and c+e < d+e, which statement is correct?
questions.explanationText: Adding the same real number preserves order, so c+e must remain greater than d+e.

questions.questionText: Given f < g, which statement is correct?
questions.explanationText: Multiplying by −3 reverses the inequality.

questions.questionText: Given h ≤ j, which statement is correct?
questions.explanationText: Subtracting the same number preserves a weak inequality.

questions.questionText: Given k > 0 and t < 0, which statement is correct?
questions.explanationText: A positive times a negative is negative.

questions.questionText: P @ Q means P > Q, P # Q means P ≤ Q, P $ Q means P = Q. Interpret P @ Q # R. Which conclusion follows?

options.text: P and R cannot be ordered with certainty

questions.explanationText: P @ Q # R translates to P>Q and Q≤R. Therefore, P>R must hold.

questions.questionText: P * Q means P < Q, P % Q means P ≥ Q, P ! Q means P = Q. Interpret A * B % C. Which conclusion follows?

options.text: A and C cannot be ordered with certainty

questions.explanationText: A * B % C translates to A<B and B≥C. Therefore, A and C cannot be ordered with certainty.

questions.questionText: P ^ Q means P ≥ Q, P ~ Q means P < Q, P = Q means P = Q. Interpret M ^ N ~ T. Which conclusion follows?

options.text: M and T cannot be ordered with certainty

questions.explanationText: M ^ N ~ T translates to M≥N and N<T. Therefore, M and T cannot be ordered with certainty.

questions.questionText: P @ Q means P ≤ Q, P # Q means P > Q, P $ Q means P = Q. Interpret X $ Y # Z. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanationText: X $ Y # Z translates to X=Y and Y>Z. Therefore, X>Z.

questions.questionText: P ! Q means P < Q, P & Q means P ≤ Q, P % Q means P > Q. Interpret D ! E & F. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanationText: D ! E & F translates to D<E and E≤F. Therefore, D<F.

questions.questionText: Given L > M ≥ N. Conclusions: I. L > N  II. M > N. Which option is correct?
questions.explanationText: L>N is forced, but M may equal N.

questions.questionText: Given A ≤ B < C. Conclusions: I. A < C  II. A < B. Which option is correct?
questions.explanationText: A<C is certain, while A may equal B.

questions.questionText: Given P = Q > R. Conclusions: I. P > R  II. Q > R. Which option is correct?
questions.explanationText: P=Q and both are greater than R.

questions.questionText: Given X ≥ Y ≥ Z. Conclusions: I. X > Z  II. X ≥ Z. Which option is correct?
questions.explanationText: X≥Z is certain, but equality throughout is possible.

questions.questionText: Given C < D = E. Conclusions: I. C < E  II. D > C. Which option is correct?
questions.explanationText: C<D=E makes both conclusions true.

questions.questionText: Given F > G < H. Conclusions: I. F > H  II. F = H. Which option is correct?
questions.explanationText: F and H both exceed G, but their relation is unknown.

questions.questionText: Given J ≤ K > L. Conclusions: I. J < L  II. K > J. Which option is correct?
questions.explanationText: J versus L is unknown, and J may equal K.

questions.questionText: Given R < S ≤ T. Conclusions: I. R < T  II. T > R. Which option is correct?
questions.explanationText: Both conclusions express the strict relation forced by the chain.

questions.questionText: Given U ≥ V = W. Conclusions: I. U ≥ W  II. V ≤ U. Which option is correct?
questions.explanationText: V=W and U≥V establish both.

questions.questionText: Given B > C ≥ D. Conclusions: I. B > D  II. C < D. Which option is correct?
questions.explanationText: B>D follows; C<D contradicts C≥D.

questions.explanationText: Team A completed 84; Team B completed 0.68×125=85.

questions.questionText: Machine P produced 480 units with 3% rejected; Q produced 470 with 1% rejected. Which had more accepted units?
questions.explanationText: Accepted outputs are 480×0.97=465.6 and 470×0.99=465.3.

questions.questionText: Plan X uses 18% less than 500 kWh; Plan Y uses 405 kWh. Compare usage.
questions.explanationText: Plan X uses 500×0.82=410 kWh, which exceeds 405.

questions.explanationText: Store A charges 2,000×0.85=1,700.

questions.questionText: Server A uptime is 99.5% of 720 hours; Server B is up 717 hours. Which is greater?
questions.explanationText: A is up 720×0.995=716.4 hours, below 717.

questions.questionText: Student P scores 72% of 250; Q scores 178. Compare scores.
Inventory falls 12% from 800 units. Compare the remainder with 700.
questions.explanationText: 800×0.88=704, which is above 700.

questions.questionText: A temperature changes from −4°C to 3°C; another rises by 6°C. Which increase is larger?
questions.explanationText: 3−(−4)=7°C, greater than 6°C.

questions.questionText: A file is compressed by 35% from 200 MB. Compare it with a 128 MB file.
Line A makes 52 units/hour for 7 hours; B makes 360 units. Which output is greater?
questions.explanationText: 52×7=364, exceeding 360.

questions.questionText: A battery at 80% of 75 Wh is compared with 58 Wh. Which is greater?
A distance is reduced 8% from 250 km; compare with 232 km.
questions.explanationText: 250×0.92=230 km, which is less than 232.

questions.questionText: Revenue A is ₹1.2 lakh increased by 5%; B is ₹1.25 lakh. Which is greater?
Data use A is 3/5 of 40 GB; B is 23.8 GB. Which is greater?
A class average is 7.5/10; another is 74%. Which is higher?
A part measures 12.04 mm; upper limit is 12.0 mm. What relation holds?
questions.explanationText: 12.04 is 0.04 greater than 12.0.

questions.questionText: Cost A falls from 900 by 20%; cost B is 725. Which is lower?
A network sends 2.5 GB/min for 8 min; another sends 19.5 GB. Which is greater?
